keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria draws this land inside the Seleucid Empire; its 164 shape hands the east to Parthia, which the seleucid-empire dossier repairs). Same Media spec as that dossier. No area on the pages.

correction.text: Media and Babylonia, where Timarchus tried to extend his realm into Babylonia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Babylonia added. The pages do not date it: 161 is the seleucid-empire dossier's year.

ledger.note: 163 BCE: Timarchus, satrap of Media since 175, makes himself king. 'In the turmoil following the death of Antiochus IV during a Persian campaign in 164 BC' he rose in Media; infobox reign 163-160. The pages do not date the proclamation more closely.
163 BCE: Media leaves Seleucid rule under its satrap. 'He was appointed satrap of Media in western Iran when Antiochus IV Epiphanes became king in 175 BC'.

161 BCE: Timarchus takes Babylonia. 'Timarchus apparently declared himself an independent king and tried to extend his realm into Babylonia; astronomical-calendar records of his reign survive (Timarchus page). Both pages are silent on the year: 161 follows the seleucid-empire dossier.
160 BCE: Demetrius I marches against him. The page gives only the end: 'Demetrius defeated and killed Timarchus in 160 BC'; the campaign's start is not dated.
160 BCE: Demetrius defeats and kills Timarchus, and the Babylonians give him the title Soter. 'Demetrius defeated and killed Timarchus in 160 BC, and dethroned Ariarathes, king of Cappadocia.'
160 BCE: Media and Babylonia return to the Seleucids. 'Demetrius defeated and killed Timarchus in 160 BC, and the Seleucid empire was temporarily united again.'
160 BCE: the rebel kingdom ends with Timarchus's death; his brother Heracleides later 'avenged him and backed the pretender Alexander Balas'.

wars.name: Demetrius I's war against Timarchus
wars.outcome: Demetrius I defeated and killed Timarchus in 160 BC and 'dethroned Ariarathes, king of Cappadocia'; Rome indirectly supported those who wanted to divide the Seleucid Empire, Timarchus among them (the page's sense).
wars.note: Demetrius took the throne around November 162; the pages date neither the revolt nor the Roman support.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; Media and Babylonia are the regions named.

notes: Two pages (budget 1-2; the rebel is not in Cliopatria). The pages date only the infobox reign (163-160), Demetrius I's accession (about November 162) and Timarchus's death (160); the Babylonian gain (161), the Roman alliance and the year of the proclamation are not dated. The seleucid-empire dossier (me-05-c) opens the loss in 161 at confidence 1; this dossier opens the state in 163 (the infobox). Ecbatana as seat is unverified. The Media spec subtracts Atropatene's Cliopatria shape of -170 as that dossier does.
